items.title: Cardinality seems inaccurate
items.body:
Possibly due to the recent change to use the datasketches crate, our cardinality seems very inaccurate for very small values. (where it should really be exact).

~~Also for large values, the datasketches crate relies on u32 coupon, harming precision for high cardinalities.~~ <- this made no sense.

items.title: Indexer panics
items.body:
**Describe the bug**
- Inserting u64 values into a date field makes index writer panic `called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ErrorInThread("An index writer was killed.. A worker thread encountered an error (io::Error most likely) or panicked.")`
- Indexer panicked 
- Indexing should not panic.

**Which version of tantivy are you using?**

0.22.0

**To Reproduce**

https://github.com/Barre/tantivy_indexing_panic_date_reproduction/blob/master/src/main.rs

items.title: "Internal error: Couldn't find term_id 25777562 in dict" for very large dicts (>20mio)
items.body:
As reported by a user:

... Since that showed promised, I tried increasing split_num_docs_target to 20 million. However, my index appears to be corrupt and is returning the following error on queries:

internal error: (internal error: tantivy error: Internal error: 'Couldn't find term_id 25777562 in dict'`, split_id: 01J3KRXAEWJ6QP0TXSSW89HR48),...

items.title: Improve incorrect type handling on columnar
monotonic mapping broken for `get_docids_for_value_range`
NaN sucks
items.body: We should prevent the usage of NaN as an input. Probably the easiest way is to drop those value on input.

items.title: Remove empty columns, remove legacy u64/i64 API?
items.body:
Related to #1890 . Maybe we should simply never write columns with no values.

This means we need to drop the methods in fastfield reader that return a Column (and not a Option<Column>)

items.title: min/max value is NaN for empty f64 columns
items.body:
As mentioned in the title and tested in `test_empty_column_f64`.

This is not a good spec because min/max is something for which we want PartialOrd to make sense.
I think we should never accept NaN and never return NaN

items.title: Add reverse dictionary streaming
items.body: When the user requests a term aggregation with `min_doc_count == 0` and sorting by keys in descending order, we need to stream the dictionary in reverse order to fill up hits

items.title: Check token constraints
items.body:
tantivy assumes tokens supplied by tokenstreams and pretokenized strings 
are sorted by token pos
Let's make sure this is enforced correctly.

items.title: Stale adding documents if there are too many ongoing merge
items.body: Following #677 we should have a way to stale indexing if there are too many ongoing merge threads.

items.title: Slope value unexpected in multilinear interpolation
Ensure that segment cannot exceed 2^31 documents.
items.body:
Tantivy requires that DocId never reach 2^31.

Right now nothing prevents a merge operation to reach this value.
This is a very unlikely thing to happen, but we should detect and avoid starting such a merge operation, (and log a warning).

items.title: Correct way of quering against "title" and "body"
items.body:
I want to query something like `Michael Jackson` and search in two fields: `title` and `body`.
I do it this way:
``` rust
 let query_parser = QueryParser::for_index(&index, vec![title, body]);
```

But the results are not relevant at all. Seems like tantivy searches only `Michael` or `Jackson` and sometimes both. I expect that documents with title containing `Michael Jackson` would be on the first line, but they are placed on say 5-th.

Then I concatenate `title` and `body` with space in one field - `body`. 
So I query like this:
``` rust
 let query_parser = QueryParser::for_index(&index, vec![body]);
```
And now the results are relevant - all docs with `Michael Jackson` in title are placed on the first lines.
Do I misunderstand something or is it a bug?

items.title: Ignore phrase query when the field does not have positions.
Handle segment file deletion in the middle of load searcher.
